activeCoveredMeaning: active-covered means the current repo has focused adapter/runtime proof and durable operator/source-of-truth evidence for the declared local or Testcontainers profile. It does not mean managed cloud operations, real cluster failover, or L5/L6 chaos proof is complete.

patterns.name: Committed dataset version remains serving truth
patterns.reason: Metadata DB committed dataset versions remain the serving truth even when S3, Iceberg, Spark, or CDC artifacts exist.

patterns.name: Search and CDC projections cannot become source of truth
patterns.reason: Object store and committed dataset state are re-read before sensitive object/search/action decisions.

patterns.name: Dangerous failures leave durable operator evidence
patterns.reason: Adapter, auth, secret, and commit-point failures must be visible in run/error/audit/outbox/trace evidence, not only logs. S56 proves read-only detector reports can surface missing-data, lag, skew, and SLO evidence before source-of-truth rows are mutated. S57 proves backup/restore preflight can block DB/storage committed-version mismatches, mark search as rebuildable projection evidence, keep outbox retry/reprocess closed while restore mode is active, and reject publisher resume until post-restore closed-loop evidence exists. S58A proves local JWT/OIDC bearer-token failures are denied before a Principal is built, M2M service-account tokens remain tenant-scoped, revoked JWT ids are blocked, JWKS refresh/cache behavior is tested, webhook signing secrets are read through SecretProvider and redacted from operator evidence/errors, and REST connector credential secretRefs are re-resolved on the next snapshot after local rotation.

patterns.name: Active stack features retest together
patterns.reason: S3, Iceberg, Spark, and Debezium CDC cannot advance as isolated happy paths once they are active together.

patterns.name: Materialization watermarks are replayable
patterns.reason: Current materialization outputs pin enough cursor state to retry without skipping or duplicating successful rows.

patterns.name: Schema drift is blocked before runtime mismatch
patterns.reason: The schema revision guard protects SQLAlchemy metadata snapshots, fresh Alembic upgrade parity proves a blank DB can reach the current table/column shape, S55 schema migration safety keeps Alembic history single-headed, blocks destructive downgrade schema operations, and now requires phase-tagged expand migrations to declare an old-and-new-app release compatibility window. S55 migration runner proof keeps Alembic execution behind a dedicated singleton DB lock and leaves password-masked operator evidence when a migration attempt fails. Dataset schema evolution proof now blocks rename/drop/narrowing-style consumer breaks, records widening/deprecated-field warnings, and creates deterministic backfill progress metadata. Ontology migration proof now blocks property/object/link/action parameter breaking changes before activation, records object reindex plans, and checks generated SDK compatibility. Live PostgreSQL contention proof, full old/new app deployment windows, actual ontology migration executors/reindex workers, real backfill execution, and rollback/restore runbook rehearsal remain broader S55 work.

patterns.name: Bad records are quarantined and replayed independently
patterns.reason: S47 now has stream CDC quarantine plus Operations API, typed generated SDK, and Web Operations UI coverage for tenant-scoped dead_letter_records, single and bulk replay idempotency, valid-payload APPEND replay result, replay failure result, discard, audit evidence, DLQ-write fail-closed tests, source-side error threshold fail-closed policy, identity/ordering fail-closed policy, and PostgreSQL concurrent replay request proof. Transform-level Record DLQ policy remains future if transform record DLQ is introduced.

patterns.name: Late data and watermark movement are explicit
patterns.reason: S48 now has a stream/source archive slice: StreamArchiveConfig declares event/source time fields, named timezone override, and lateness thresholds, committed archive rows separate event/source/ingest/process time with a late_data_status, too-late records route to Record DLQ, transaction metadata keeps a matching partition/source lateDataWatermark from moving backward without letting unrelated fast-partition watermarks classify slow partitions as stale, duplicate delivery after a committed late event resumes from the durable offset instead of creating a second dataset version, late stream commits expose lateDataSummary plus lateDataReprocessingPlan through Operations run detail, materialization commits expose watermark plus late-data reopen evidence when a LATE_REQUIRES_REPROCESS CDC index run forces the next closed output to be regenerated, object/materialization explain exposes late-data badges, Operations detail exposes a downstream impact graph for the regenerated materialization, and a late stale CDC delete cannot remove or resurrect the current active object.

patterns.name: Dataset readers use the committed manifest file list
patterns.reason: S49 now has a read/preview slice: DatasetStorageAdapter.data_file_paths resolves manifest-listed data files in order, foundry.datasets.preview reads multi-file manifests through the existing facade, unlisted files in the storage directory are not discovered by listing, dataset rows can declare layout policy fields, local/fake/S3 read/preview partition filters reduce actual read files, and Iceberg skips reads when no manifest file matches. Multi-part atomic commit, transform predicate pushdown, high-cardinality partition warnings, and Iceberg snapshot file-level pruning remain future work.

patterns.name: Iceberg maintenance does not delete serving snapshots
patterns.reason: S50 now has a maintenance planning slice: Operations can request an Iceberg maintenance plan, committed DB dataset-version snapshots are marked protected, compaction candidates are reported from file-count/small-file/read-amplification thresholds, and the plan request leaves audit evidence. Actual rewrite_data_files execution, snapshot expiration, and orphan cleanup remain future work.

patterns.name: CDC archive workers can run bounded continuous loops
patterns.reason: S51 now has a bounded continuous stream archive worker loop that repeatedly calls the existing archive_stream_events transaction boundary, stops after configured empty polls or a stop callback, and reports loop summary counts. Lease fencing, rebalance revocation, commit-unknown reconciliation, and a continuous CDC object-index worker remain future work.

patterns.name: Product workflows execute through Temporal
patterns.reason: ConnectorSyncWorkflow now has a product workflow control-plane path through Operations/API/SDK with local/fake/Temporal contract proof and audit-linked ProductWorkflowRun evidence. Real connector activity data-plane execution, cancellation cleanup, response-loss reconciliation, continue-as-new, upgrade replay, and managed worker operations remain future work.

patterns.name: External writeback uses saga and reconciliation evidence
patterns.reason: S53 now has simulated before-commit writeback slices where response loss becomes outcome_unknown, external success followed by local mutation failure becomes compensation_required, and operator-provided remote-success resolve catches up the local object mutation while closing action/writeback evidence as reconciled. Same-idempotency-key replay does not blindly issue another writeback, concurrent reconcile has one winner, and sensitive writeback parameters stay masked in Operations/audit surfaces. Real vendor APIs, vendor remote lookup, compensation worker execution, persistent reconciliation queue, and operator approval remain future work.

patterns.name: Dataset quality uses versioned contract evidence
patterns.reason: S54 first slices record the staged candidate fingerprint and schema row/version used by dataset quality check results through checked_manifest_hash, validated_against_schema_version_id, and validated_against_schema_version. Historical check results stay pinned to the schema row/version used by that run after later schema versions are created. Successful check rows are stored as PASS, warning severity failures are visible as non-blocking WARN, and staged candidate tamper or commit-time hard failure is rejected as BLOCK_COMMIT before storage commit. Row-level not_null/unique quarantine checks route failed records to tenant-scoped Record DLQ as DATA_QUALITY_CONTRACT, rewrite the staged candidate to clean records, and revalidate before commit. Operations run detail exposes the transaction-scoped quality summary, schema references, checked manifest hashes, check results, and up to 5 data-quality quarantine failed-row samples. Full DataContract CRUD, owner notification, dedicated failed-row sample UI, quality history/trend, and production DB schema race proof remain future work.

patterns.name: Frontend and agents never bypass public API or SDK
patterns.reason: The generated SDK and Object Explorer use public surfaces, but the full S61-S64 workspace track is not complete.

patterns.name: Flink runner
patterns.reason: Flink remains outside the current S46 execution path.
patterns.notApplicableReason: Spark is the current compute ratchet; Flink is explicitly deferred until a later compute-family decision.
